description: Somos un equipo multidisciplinario apasionado por la innovación tecnológica, la ciencia de datos y la sostenibilidad. Nuestro objetivo es desarrollar soluciones que integren datos satelitales de la NASA, análisis estadístico, inteligencia artificial y modelos predictivos para mejorar la toma de decisiones agrícolas frente al cambio climático. Contamos con habilidades en programación, modelado estadístico y visualización de datos. Valoramos la creatividad, la colaboración y el impacto global.
summary: TerraScope is a bilingual web app that helps anyone tell whether a change in Earth's climate is a real trend or just noise, for their own place. The user picks a point on a 3D planet, or one of Peru's lakes such as Lake Titicaca, and the app pulls NASA data, runs three trend tests (Sen's slope, Mann-Kendall, least squares) and explains each result in plain language, like a detective's case file. A traffic light rates risk from 0 to 100 with its confidence under three possible futures, and a time slider with a thermometer shows what the series projects through 2050. Every figure carries its period and source, projections are validated against the past, and practice data is always labelled as not real measurements. Our goal is to make NASA's open data usable by communities, authorities and students who need to decide, not only to read numbers.
details:
What it does. TerraScope has five connected sections. Explore scans 30 places on a 3D planet and shows where a variable rises or falls, with false-discovery-rate control. Lab runs trend analysis with three tests, plus decomposition, anomalies, forecast and early-warning signals. Lakes holds an inventory of Peru's lakes with a precipitation-minus-evaporation balance and scenarios. Decide gives a traffic-light risk score with confidence, three futures, actions by audience (authority, farming and community, research) and an evidence passport (JSON, CSV, printable report). Learn offers a six-lesson route, glossary and quiz. A sentinel agent re-checks the lakes periodically, and the mascot Killa explains charts in four short sentences.

Scientific honesty. The balance is rainfall minus evaporation in a cell of about 50 km, not a measured lake level. Projections are conditional on the past trend continuing, are not predictions, and are checked by hiding the last five years. The AI never calculates: it only interprets numbers computed by the statistical code, and a figure the app did not compute is discarded. Practice data is always labelled as not real measurements.

Tools. React 18, Vite, Mantine, Zustand, CesiumJS (3D planet), ECharts, Plotly, D3 and Observable Plot, deployed on Vercel. The statistics were written for this project.

Creativity and impact. It turns a hard statistical question into a guided investigation for non-experts, tied to a place close to us (Lake Titicaca), in two languages and on any device.

Limits and next steps. We do not yet measure water surface area from satellite images (the app only queries the scene catalogue), and the risk score still needs validation with real dry events.

AI use. Code and text were developed with assistance from Claude (Anthropic). The in-app assistant Killa uses a large language model.
